strategy: Extract Discount behavior to an IDiscountStrategy and use composition (Strategy Pattern). Remove behavior-throwing overrides in VIPCustomer.
steps: 1) Introduce interface `IDiscountStrategy` with `double GetDiscount(CustomerContext ctx)`.
2) Implement `VipDiscountStrategy` that contains VIP-specific discount logic previously (or a thin adapter to new DiscountManager).
3) Change `Customer` to hold an `IDiscountStrategy` (default strategy) and delegate discount calculation to it; mark `GetDiscount()` non-virtual or delegate implementation.
4) Modify `VipCustomer` to compose `IDiscountStrategy` instead of overriding `GetDiscount()` (assign VipDiscountStrategy via ctor).
5) Update call sites to use `customer.GetDiscount()` unchanged — behavior preserved via strategy delegation.
6) Add unit tests ensuring VIP discount path uses VipDiscountStrategy and does not throw.
7) Remove obsolete override in `VipCustomer` once tests pass.
8) Document the new extension point for future VIP-like customers.
tests.risk: Medium - touches public API (Customer ctor/behavior) and requires updating any custom subclasses that relied on virtual overrides. Mitigation: keep default virtual wrapper for transition and run unit tests.

tests.strategy: Replace behavioral exceptions with role-based capabilities (Interface Segregation + Null Object/Policy). Implement separate IOrderApprovalPolicy and IAlcoholPolicy injected into customers.
steps: 1) Define `IOrderApprovalPolicy` with `bool CanMakePurchase(CustomerContext ctx)` and `void RequestApproval(...)`.
2) Define `IAlcoholPolicy` with `bool CanOrderAlcohol(CustomerContext ctx)`.
3) Provide `MinorApprovalPolicy` and `MinorAlcoholPolicy` implementations that return false for minors and optionally provide a RequestApproval flow (no exceptions).
4) Make `Customer` accept these policy interfaces via ctor (with defaults for adults).
5) Modify `MinorCustomer` to supply minor-specific policies instead of throwing in overrides.
6) Update any callers of MakePurchase()/CanOrderAlcohol() to check policy results rather than catching exceptions.
7) Add unit tests verifying minors are blocked but no exceptions bubble up and that approval flow triggers correctly.
8) Deprecate and remove exception-throwing overrides after validation.
tests.risk: Low-Medium - replaces exceptions with policied behavior; callers that relied on exception handling must be updated. Add adapter wrappers during migration.

tests.strategy: Split responsibilities: keep `Customer` as a thin data holder and move behaviors into small focused interfaces (IDiscountProvider, IPurchaseService, IAlcoholPolicy, ILoyaltyCalculator). (Single Responsibility + Interface Segregation)
steps: 1) Create lightweight DTO `CustomerContext` with properties used by behavior logic (Age, VisitCount, MembershipLevel, etc.).
2) Extract `IDiscountProvider`, `IPurchaseService`, `IAlcoholPolicy`, `ILoyaltyCalculator` interfaces and implement default production classes.
3) Refactor `Customer` to be a simple holder for identity and references to these services or to get them passed when needed (prefer composition over inheritance).
4) Replace existing virtual methods with delegating calls to injected services (constructor injection or method args).
5) Update `MinorCustomer`/`VipCustomer` to supply different service implementations instead of overriding many methods.
6) Add unit tests per service to cover behaviors (discounts, purchase flow, alcohol policy, loyalty multipliers).
7) Run integration tests to confirm no functional regressions.
tests.risk: High - API reshaping that changes how callers obtain behavior. Mitigation: provide adapter shims that forward to old virtual methods while migrating. Keep changes incremental.

tests.strategy: Introduce focused role interfaces (IOrderable, IAlcoholConsumer) and have `Customer` implement small interfaces or be composed with capability objects. (Interface Segregation)
steps: 1) Define `IOrderable` with `MakePurchase(CustomerContext ctx)` and `IAlcoholConsumer` with `bool CanOrderAlcohol(CustomerContext ctx)`.
2) Refactor `Customer` to expose capabilities via composition: `IOrderable Orderable { get; }`, etc.
3) Provide default implementations and specialized ones for `MinorCustomer`/`EmployeeCustomer` etc.
4) Update callers to depend on specific interfaces rather than the whole `Customer` type.
5) Add tests for each capability to ensure behavior preserved.
tests.risk: Medium - improves design but requires adjusting callers to use interfaces. Use adapter methods for backwards compatibility.

tests.strategy: Decompose `DiscountManager` into smaller components: Rule objects (Strategy/Specification), PriceCatalog, ReceiptFormatter, LoyaltyCalculator, and Notification services. (Single Responsibility + Open/Closed)
steps: 1) Extract a `PriceCatalog` service that owns item prices (dictionary) and lookup methods.
2) Extract `IDiscountRule` interface and move each large conditional block into discrete rule classes implementing `bool IsApplicable(CustomerContext)` and `double Calculate(CustomerContext)`.
3) Create `DiscountEngine` that composes a list of `IDiscountRule` and computes total discount by iterating rules — rules can be registered/added without changing engine.
4) Move `GenerateReceipt()` responsibilities into `ReceiptFormatter` class which takes computed values and formats strings.
5) Move `CalculateLoyaltyPoints()` into `LoyaltyCalculator` interface implementation.
6) Add constructor injection and remove public mutable fields in favor of an immutable `CustomerContext` parameter passed to engine/formatter.
7) Add tests for each rule, the engine aggregation, price lookups and receipt formatting.
8) Run integration tests and replace the big `CalculateDiscount()` with `new DiscountEngine(rules).Calculate(ctx)`.
tests.risk: Medium-High - large decomposition but low behavioral-change risk if rules are ported carefully and covered by tests. Start by creating thin adapters that call original methods until migrated.

tests.strategy: Make discount rules pluggable by implementing `IDiscountRule` and register rules using configuration or factories (Open/Closed).
steps: 1) Extract major switch/if blocks into classes implementing `IDiscountRule` (e.g., `BurgerComboRule`, `VIPMembershipRule`, `PromoCodeRule`).
2) Implement a `DiscountRuleFactory` that provides rule instances from config or DI container.
3) Replace the monolithic switch logic with `foreach (var r in rules) if (r.IsApplicable(ctx)) total += r.Calculate(ctx);`.
4) Provide unit tests for each rule class and an integration test for the rule set order/interaction.
5) Document how to add new rules without modifying engine code.
tests.risk: Low-Medium - porting complexity concentrated in rule implementations; mitigated by one-to-one mapping tests.

tests.strategy: Centralize pricing in a `PriceCatalog` and remove magic numbers across codebase; use catalog lookups in engine, formatter and order processor (Single Responsibility + Open/Closed).
steps: 1) Add `IPriceCatalog` with `double GetPrice(string item)` and an implementation `InMemoryPriceCatalog` seeded from a single source.
2) Replace ItemPrices initializations and hardcoded price switches with calls to `_priceCatalog.GetPrice(item)` in `GenerateReceipt()` and `OrderProcessor`.
3) Add unit tests ensuring price lookups match expected constants and that adding an item only requires updating the catalog.
4) Optionally move price data to config/JSON to allow editing without code changes.
5) Remove duplicated magic literals after tests pass.
tests.risk: Low - straightforward refactor; main risk is missing a place where a magic number was used in a different semantic way. Comprehensive search and tests mitigate.

tests.strategy: Introduce abstractions for external communication (IEmailSender, ISmsSender, IDatabase) and inject via DI (Dependency Inversion).
steps: 1) Define `IEmailSender.Send(to, subject, body)` and `ISmsSender.Send(phone, message)` and `IOrderRepository.Save(order)` interfaces.
2) Implement `ConsoleEmailSender`/`ConsoleSmsSender` for local/dev usage and production adapters for real providers.
3) Replace `SendEmailReceipt`/`SendSmsReceipt` bodies with calls to injected interfaces and remove hardcoded SMTP strings.
4) Update `OrderProcessor` to accept interfaces via ctor instead of `new`ing concrete services.
5) Add unit tests using mocks (e.g., Moq) to verify interactions without touching external systems.
tests.risk: Low-Medium - adds abstraction layer; must ensure adapters for existing behavior and configuration for production endpoints. Using Console adapters preserves current behavior during migration.

tests.strategy: Split `IPaymentProcessor` into multiple focused interfaces (IHandlesCash, IHandlesCard, IHandlesPaypal...) and apply Interface Segregation, then adapt implementations.
steps: 1) Create small interfaces: `ICashProcessor { void ProcessCash(double) }`, `ICardProcessor { void ProcessCreditCard(...); void ProcessDebitCard(...); }`, `IPaypalProcessor { void ProcessPaypal(...); }`, etc.
2) Update existing `CashPaymentProcessor` to implement `ICashProcessor` only.
3) Update any callers to depend on the specific interface they need (e.g., use ICashProcessor when cash processing is required).
4) Provide an adapter `CompositePaymentProcessor` if any code expects a single entrypoint; adapter delegates to specific processors.
5) Add tests verifying a CashProcessor does not require unimplemented methods and that CompositePaymentProcessor correctly routes calls.
6) Deprecate `IPaymentProcessor` gradually or keep as facade implemented by CompositePaymentProcessor.
tests.risk: Low - interface segregation isolates changes; main risk is updating all callers. Provide Composite facade for backward compatibility.

tests.strategy: Make CashPaymentProcessor adhere to its (now segregated) interface or provide an adapter; ensure no NotImplementedException escapes (Liskov).
steps: 1) After Interface Segregation, ensure `CashPaymentProcessor` only implements `ICashProcessor` and remove unimplemented members.
2) If code needs a full-featured processor, add `CompositePaymentProcessor` that aggregates specialized processors and implements the legacy facade.
3) Add unit tests ensuring `CashPaymentProcessor` does not throw for its documented contract and that `CompositePaymentProcessor` routes calls appropriately.
4) Replace any `new CashPaymentProcessor()` usages where a full facade is needed with `CompositePaymentProcessor` constructed from specific processors.
tests.risk: Low - straightforward; ensure backward compatibility with Composite facade.

tests.strategy: Extract receipt formatting to `ReceiptFormatter` and separate calculation from presentation (Single Responsibility).
steps: 1) Create `ReceiptFormatter.Format(CustomerContext ctx, double discount, double tax, double total)` returning string.
2) Move string-building code from `GenerateReceipt()` into `ReceiptFormatter` implementation.
3) Make `DiscountManager.GenerateReceipt()` call the engine to compute values and pass them to the formatter.
4) Add unit tests comparing formatted output lines (or using substring matches) to ensure formatting unchanged.
5) Optionally add templating support for easier changes.
tests.risk: Low - separates format from logic; verify formatting unit tests to keep outputs identical.

tests.strategy: Move demo/test code out of production `Program.cs` into a test harness or separate sample app; keep Program focused on application startup (Single Responsibility).
steps: 1) Create `samples/` or `examples/` folder and move demo usage (dm1..dm4) into `Samples.cs` or a test project under `tests/`.
2) Reduce `Program.cs` to minimal bootstrap code calling into application services or launching samples via a debug flag.
3) Add unit/integration tests that replicate the scenarios formerly in `Program.cs` so behavior is preserved.
4) Ensure CI does not execute demo scenarios as part of normal test runs (use a separate test category).
tests.diff:
--- a/ApocalypticFastFood/ApocalypticFastFood/Program.cs
+++ b/ApocalypticFastFood/ApocalypticFastFood/Program.cs
@@
-// demo scenarios and tests in Main
-Console.WriteLine(
tests.risk: Low - cosmetic and organizational; minimal runtime risk. Ensure demo scenarios moved to tests to preserve validation.
